name: Maine

office.name: Maine BMV Motor Carrier Services - Overlimit Permit Unit

fees.note: Ch. 156 Table 1 (excess over 80,000 lb for 5+ axle combos). Maine charges only the highest of the weight/length/width/height fees (grouped), not the sum - summing lines would overstate multi-limit loads by a few dollars.
Ch. 156 Table 3 (excess width over 102 in, in 1-ft bands after the first 2 ft). Only the highest component fee is actually charged (Ch. 156 §4).
Ch. 156 Table 4 (excess height over 14 ft). Only the highest component fee is actually charged (Ch. 156 §4).

Ch. 156 Table 2, bands measured from 74 ft (TT + 48-53 ft semitrailer). Legal base is 65 ft for other combos / 69 ft with <=48 ft trailer, which shifts the bands. Only the highest component fee is actually charged (Ch. 156 §4).

escorts.when: Over 12' wide, on interstates and freeways
Over 12' wide, on two-lane and other roads
Over 80' long, on interstates and freeways
Over 80' long, on two-lane and other roads

police.text: 1 police escort. 16 ft or wider: 1 police + 1 pilot (2 police when MSP/MaineDOT/BMV deem necessary). State Police required on the Interstate system.
1 police escort. 125 ft or longer: 1 police + 1 pilot. State Police required on the Interstate system.
1 police escort. Rear overhang over 15 ft: 1 police + 1 pilot.
2 police escorts. 20 ft or wider: 2 police + 1 pilot; utility/town notification, no commuter or school-bus hours.
2 police escorts. 150 ft or longer: 2 police + 1 pilot; permittee does public outreach (press release, municipal notice).

restrictions.text: Daylight only: 30 min before sunrise to 30 min after sunset, Monday-Friday. April 22-November 18: Saturday until 12 PM; June 3-August 26: Saturday on I-95 only until 9 AM (other roads until 12 PM). No travel on holidays or holiday weekends; Sundays in July/August and holidays need MaineDOT Traffic Engineering pre-clearance.
No movement in poor visibility or on roads made dangerous by rain, snow, slush or ice. If Interstate speed is reduced to 45 mph, exit at the first opportunity.
20 ft+ wide (or 150 ft+ long): utility and town notifications, clear visibility only, no movement during commuter or school-bus hours.
150 ft+ long: utility/town notifications, clear visibility only, no commuter or school-bus hours; permittee must do public outreach (press release, municipal notification).
Overweight-only permits that can move with the flow of traffic may travel at any time of day.

travel.weekends: No travel Saturday afternoon or Sunday
travel.holidays: No travel from noon the day before through the holiday; a Monday or Friday holiday closes the long weekend
travel.note: Saturday until noon only Apr 22-Nov 18; outside that window no Saturday travel.

sources.title: 29-250 CMR Ch. 156 - Fee Structure for Over Dimensional and Overweight Loads, along with State Police Escort Fee (filing 2010-281)
29-250 CMR Ch. 157 - The Administration of Over Dimension and Overweight Permits (filing 2025-033)
Maine BMV Motor Carrier Services Manual (rev. Aug 2016), Part VI

notes: Ch. 156 §4: if more than one limit is exceeded, only the single highest fee ($6.00-$27.50) is charged. The calculator sums the weight/width/height/length lines, so multi-limit loads are overstated (worst case ~4x). Verify actual permit fee with the Overlimit Permit Unit.
Fee tables are from the 2010 Ch. 156 rule (still the current version listed by the Secretary of State); statute §2382(2) caps single-trip fees at $6-$30.
The Maine Turnpike needs its own oversize/overweight permit, $10 at any toll plaza plus toll (not included in the fee lines).
State Police escorts are billed at actual cost by DPS with a 4-hour minimum; arrange directly with MSP at least 3 working days ahead; police-escort permits generally not issued for Saturdays.

Pilot positions: one pilot travels in front on undivided highways and behind on divided highways (modeled interstate=rear, non_interstate=front). Rear-overhang 5-15 ft needs 2 pilots; over 15 ft needs police + 1 pilot (calculator may show 2 pilots + police).
Routine overweight ceilings without detailed MaineDOT review: 5-axle TT 130,000 lb, 6-axle 140,000 lb, 7-axle 159,000-167,000 lb, 8-axle 177,000 lb; heavier is an extreme load.

New England Transportation Consortium (NETC) multi-state permit available for loads within 90' long, 13'6" high, 14' wide, 108,000 lb (5-axle) / 120,000 lb (6+ axle TT-semi); larger loads need separate state permits.
State permits cover MaineDOT roads only; local roads need town/municipal permission.
